cross_cutting_findings.description: Direct exec.run plus TOTP and task-system signed exact-draft permits are intentionally separate authorization routes with different callers and ownership. The final sender enforces a signed single-use task-dispatch permit when that option is used, while six-digit TOTP is enforced by the caller's exec trust gate rather than send.py; the active route and final-executor gate are unknown. The installer removes message.send from requireApproval.
cross_cutting_findings.required_proof: Live final executor call path, active config gate, account, exact draft/permit ownership, sent-item readback, and owner decision on contract alignment.

cross_cutting_findings.description: SkilzVolt hook supplies live catalogue metadata and directs full reads through the tool; local loader only scans local files. A local or ignored repair copy cannot prove live skill activation. This is an evidence boundary, not a live-skill/local-loader contradiction.
cross_cutting_findings.required_proof: Live prompt/tool trace showing selected current skill read and invoked runtime consumer.

cross_cutting_findings.description: Live reply-draft contract requires unsent Outlook Drafts with no automatic send. The tracked send executor creates/patches a reply and then calls Graph send, but no evidence establishes that send.py is used as the live draft writer; the relationship therefore remains unverified.
cross_cutting_findings.required_proof: Identify live draft writer, prove no-send execution and Drafts/conversation readback; do not infer it from the bridge adapter.
